what: oco-agent exists only as built on the lab: lab-agent's releases do not carry it, so a driver elsewhere has it by the lab's hand. Looked at before replacing (2026-11-14): it is not an oversight - release-plz.toml says oco-agent grows here beside lab-agent and is not released until it takes over. What it waits on is the switch: the daemon retiring, which waits on the author's own driving
21 release runs failed after oco-agent's crates joined the workspace, and nothing said so
countermeasure: oco-agent's crates given their own tag names (PR 156); still open within it: a failing run after a merge must be heard (backlog:release-runs-watched) And now heard: the lab says a run that fails on main within a quarter hour, and the picture shows it (working the-lab-hears-what-fails).

what: lab-agent replayed finished jobs: GitHub's directory listing stops at 1,000 entries without saying so
countermeasure: listings read from the git tree, a cut-short listing refused, every request with time limits (lab-agent 0.1.53)

what: ten repositories on the lab carried the old token in their git settings - nine in a remote address, one as the address a branch pushes to, so it was still in use - while it had been said that nothing on the lab held it: only two folders had been searched, and the claim was wider than the check. Looking printed it into a job's log
countermeasure: every git address on the lab is plain (the credential helper reaches GitHub without a secret in the address) and each was proven to reach GitHub so; the log is masked on the lab; the search now covers every git address and the usual credential and shell files. The log's earlier form stays in the private jobs repository's history: revoking the old token is what ends it.

what: the GitHub token can do far more than the lab needs - delete repositories, administer organizations and the enterprise - so whoever holds it can do all of that
the GitHub token appeared in process listings and in conversation; it must be rotated
countermeasure: rotated 2026-11-12 by the author. The new token reached the lab sealed with a one-time key made on the lab (RSA-OAEP), never in the jobs repository; installed in its two places (token, env), the voice and oco-agent restarted onto it, and the work landed through it. The assistant's helpers read it from a private file, no longer written into commands. The old token is kept aside, private, until the author revokes it. Corrected 2026-11-13: it was not true that nothing on the lab held the old token - ten git addresses did (problem the-old-token-in-git-addresses). They are plain now, and the old token can be revoked. 2026-11-13: every git setting on the lab is plain; the old token is no longer used anywhere on the lab.

what: the watcher's schedule ran once, nine hours late, then not again: GitHub's schedules are best-effort and drop silently
countermeasure: the pulse at Healthchecks is the lab's watcher; the workflow is a probe run by hand (decisions:2026-11-12-the-pulse-is-the-watcher). Its alerts reach the author's email; through ntfy once the author adds that integration in Healthchecks.
